In this case study, I use the API provided by arXiv to retrieve research paper metadata [@arxiv_api]. I used the arXiv API to retrieve up to 500 research papers matching the exact phrase "climate change" through the all search field. 

```{r}
#install.packages("httr")  # Run only once
library(httr)
library(xml2)
library(tidyverse)
```

 


```{r}
arxiv <- GET("http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:climate%20change")

status_code(arxiv)
```

  html_structure()

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(xml2)
library(tidyverse)

# --- Configuration ---
query_term    <- 'all:"climate change"'  # Change to your target search query
batch_size    <- 100            # Max allowed per request by arXiv is 30,000
total_results <- 500            # Total number of papers you want to fetch
base_url      <- "http://export.arxiv.org/api/query"

# Empty list container to store tibbles from each batch iteration
all_batches <- list()

# --- Loop Through Results ---
for (start_idx in seq(0, total_results - 1, by = batch_size)) {
  
  message(sprintf("Fetching results %d to %d...", start_idx, start_idx + batch_size - 1))
  
  # 1. Build and execute the API request
  req <- request(base_url) %>% 
    req_url_query(
      search_query = query_term,
      start = start_idx,
      max_results = batch_size
    )
  
  resp <- req_perform(req)
  xml_content <- resp_body_xml(resp)
  
  # 2. Extract elements using XML namespaces (arXiv uses the Atom 1.0 standard)
  # Strip namespaces to make standard XPath selectors easier
  xml_ns_strip(xml_content)
  
  entries <- xml_find_all(xml_content, ".//entry")
  
  # Break loop early if the API returns no more records
  if (length(entries) == 0) {
    message("No more entries found. Ending loop.")
    break
  }
  
  # 3. Parse Title and Publication Date from the current batch
  titles       <- xml_text(xml_find_all(entries, "./title"))
  pub_dates    <- xml_text(xml_find_all(entries, "./published"))
  
  # Clean up formatting strings (removes line breaks/extra spaces from titles)
  titles       <- str_squish(titles)
  pub_dates    <- as.Date(pub_dates) # Converts "2026-10-12T14:00:00Z" to date class
  
  # 4. Save current batch into our list container
  all_batches[[length(all_batches) + 1]] <- tibble(
    title = titles,
    publication_date = pub_dates
  )
  
  # 5. Respect the API Rules: arXiv requires a 3-second delay between calls
  Sys.sleep(3)
}

# --- Combine Into One Large Tibble ---
big_arxiv_tibble <- bind_rows(all_batches)

# View the final dataset
print(big_arxiv_tibble)
```
